findings.title: Prior audit evidence base deleted from the repository
findings.impact: The record of what was found, accepted, and left open was destroyed; a reader at HEAD would conclude no security or financial audit ever ran. Code fixes survive.
findings.evidence: git ls-tree 62d6c15 AUDIT/ vs HEAD; 7 docs + npm-audit.json deleted

findings.title: HEAD carried a committed file with unresolved git conflict markers
findings.location: apps/api/src/common/core/guards/authorization.guard.ts, landed via one of the two unlabelled 'update' commits (a77fa1f, 68c9f6e) on 2026-08-25
findings.impact: authorization.guard.ts as committed is not valid TypeScript (literal <<<<<<< / ||||||| / ======= / >>>>>>> markers). A fresh clone or CI checkout of main fails typecheck/build immediately. Root cause: an autostash (git stash list still shows stash@{0}) was popped mid-refactor, conflicted across ~17 files, and the manual resolution was left uncommitted (and in this one file, unstaged) while other touched files were committed as-is.
findings.evidence_detail: git show HEAD:apps/api/src/common/core/guards/authorization.guard.ts showed the raw markers; the working tree already carried a correct hand-resolved version, unstaged.
findings.note: Fixing this required finishing the refactor the conflict was in the middle of: consolidating the old apps/api/src/common/auth.ts barrel and the duplicate apps/api/src/common/guards/access-token.guard.ts into apps/api/src/common/core (which already held the canonical, current guard implementations - JWT algorithm pinned, TokenRevocationService-integrated AccessGuard), and wiring the previously-orphaned common/decorators/{authorize,public-rate-limit}.decorator.ts and common/utils/{assertion,runtime-environment}.util.ts into the common/core barrel so every module import resolves through one path. All ~17 affected files' imports verified consistent (no stale common/auth or common/errors references remain); full verify gate re-run clean: typecheck (api/web/contracts), lint (api/web), test (38 api suites/210 tests + 7 web suites/24 tests, 234 total), build (contracts/api/web) all green. A stale, unrelated autostash (stash@{0}) predating the common/core restructure and the commerce module split (diffs against apps/api/src/common/guards/authorization.guard.ts and commerce/commerce.controller.ts, paths that no longer exist) was left untouched rather than dropped or applied - flagged for the user to review.

findings.title: English locale labels Toman amounts as IRR, understating every price 10x
findings.impact: English-locale users see prices 10x lower than actual. Withdrawal form (teacher-finance.tsx:29) labels a Toman input as IRR.
findings.evidence: Canonical unit is Toman per gateway.service.ts:5-8; every web money formatter emits 'IRR' for locale en on the same integer.
findings.note: Closed by MIG-001 step 1 (centralised formatter), independent of the unit migration.
findings.regression_test: money.spec.ts 'labels the amount as Toman in both locales, never IRR (FIN-101)'

findings.title: Refund could exceed the captured amount under concurrency
findings.impact: Over-refund lands as withdrawable wallet credit. A double-click on the admin refund button was sufficient.
findings.regression_test: refunds.service.spec.ts 'runs the over-refund check at Serializable isolation (FIN-102)' - fails pre-fix, passes post-fix

findings.title: Reconciliation.providerAmount records our own gatewayAmount, not the provider's
findings.impact: Defeats the independent cross-check the Reconciliation table exists to provide; a real amount mismatch would be invisible.

verified: Baseline gates re-measured at ebdb499: typecheck/lint/test/build all green, 193 tests
No Float or Decimal on any money column in schema.prisma; all money is Int
